title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 76
paragraphs: Thus the two armies contended with one another; and Croesus, being dissatisfied with his own army as regards numbers—for the army with which he had fought was far smaller than that of Cyrus—being dissatisfied, I say, on this account, when Cyrus did not try to advance against him on the following day, marched back to Sardis. He had in mind to call upon the Egyptians for help according to the oath they had sworn (for he had made an alliance with Amasis, king of Egypt, before making the alliance with the Lacedaemonians); and to summon the Babylonians as well, for with them too an alliance had been concluded by him, Labynetus being at that time ruler of the Babylonians; and moreover to send a message to the Lacedaemonians bidding them appear at a fixed time. Then, after he had gathered all these together and had assembled his own army, his plan was to let the winter pass and at the coming of spring march against the Persians. With these thoughts in mind, as soon as he reached Sardis he proceeded to send heralds to his several allies, giving them notice that by the fifth month from that time they should assemble at Sardis. But the army he had with him, which had fought with the Persians—an army consisting of mercenary troops—he let go and disbanded altogether, never expecting that Cyrus, after having contended against him with such evenly balanced fortune, would after all march upon Sardis.
